result:
Excellent! All tests pass and typecheck succeeds. The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what was implemented:

## Comments System Implementation

### Database
- Created `comments` table with: id, post_id, user_id, body, created_at
- Created `comment_reports` table with: comment_id, user_id (unique pair)
- Both tables have CASCADE delete constraints for data integrity

### Models & Resources
- `Comment` model with author relationship
- `CommentReport` model for managing reports
- `CommentResource` for serializing comment data to API responses

### Validation & Authorization
- `CommentValidator` ensures body is 1-2000 characters
- `CommentPolicy` enforces: only signed-in users can create/report; only comment author or post author can delete; anyone else gets 403

### Endpoints
- `POST /posts/:id/comments` - Create comment (validates body, redirects to post on success)
- `DELETE /comments/:id` - Delete comment (403 if unauthorized, redirects to post on success)
- `POST /comments/:id/report` - Report comment (always returns 204, idempotent)

### Post Page
- Shows comments oldest first with author name and creation date
- Comments with 3+ reports are hidden from all viewers
- Signed-in users see comment form, delete/report buttons where appropriate
- Guests see prompt to sign in

### Cascade Behavior
- Deleting a post removes all its comments
- Deleting a comment removes all its reports

The implementation follows existing Guren patterns for models, validation, authorization, and resource serialization.
